title: What can you say about chasteberry (vitex) in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library supports 2 wordings for chasteberry (vitex); the strongest is "Helps relieve premenstrual symptoms" (moderate, 30-2,000 mg dried fruit (or extract equivalent) a day). Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Treats infertility, PCOS or endometriosis".

supported_wordings.why: Health Canada lists it as a herbal medicine use; no other listed source covers it.
supported_wordings.daily_dose: 30-2,000 mg dried fruit (or extract equivalent) a day
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adult women 18 and older; use for at least 3 months to see an effect.

supported_wordings.wording: Helps relieve menopausal symptoms such as hot flushes.
supported_wordings.why: Health Canada lists it as a herbal medicine use; no other listed source covers it.
supported_wordings.daily_dose: 30-2,000 mg dried fruit (or extract equivalent) a day

wordings_to_avoid.why: Names a disorder; the supported wording is premenstrual symptoms.

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition

sources.name: FDA final rule on structure/function statements, 65 FR 1000 (6 January 2000), page 1000

disclaimer: Not legal advice. This guide shows the wording that published evidence supports at a daily dose, from the sources linked below; it is not a ruling on any claim. Your own product, its form and dose, and your own evidence still need to match the wording you use.
